subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The shape memory alloy commonly known as Nitinol is an alloy of which two metals?
options: Nickel and titanium
Nickel and chromium
Nickel and copper
Aluminium and titanium
questions.explain: Nitinol is an alloy of nickel and titanium, which returns to a remembered shape when heated above its transition temperature.

questions.q: Thermochromic pigments change colour in response to a change in which of the following?
options: Temperature
Light level
Pressure
Moisture
questions.explain: Thermochromic materials reversibly change colour when their temperature rises or falls.

questions.q: Photochromic materials change colour in response to which stimulus?
options: Ultraviolet or light levels
An increase in temperature
An electric current
Applied mechanical force
questions.explain: Photochromic materials darken or change colour when exposed to light, particularly ultraviolet light.

questions.q: Graphene is best described as which of the following?
options: A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice
A single layer of silicon atoms in a square lattice
Many stacked layers of graphite bonded together
Carbon nanotubes wound into a solid sphere
questions.explain: Graphene is a one-atom-thick sheet of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal (honeycomb) lattice.

questions.q: Carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) is made by combining which two components?
options: Carbon fibres set within a polymer resin matrix
Carbon powder mixed into molten metal
Glass fibres set within a concrete matrix
Carbon fibres woven with natural cotton threads
questions.explain: CFRP is a composite of strong carbon fibres held together in a polymer resin matrix.

questions.q: Kevlar is a strong technical textile most commonly used to make which product?
options: Bulletproof body armour
Breathable waterproof jackets
Self-cleaning window glass
Colour-changing baby spoons
questions.explain: Kevlar is an aramid fibre with a very high strength-to-weight ratio, widely used in bulletproof body armour.

questions.q: In the context of modern materials, what does the abbreviation LCD stand for?
options: Liquid crystal display
Low carbon device
Light conducting diode
Layered ceramic disc
questions.explain: LCD stands for liquid crystal display, a modern material used in screens and displays.

questions.q: Why are shape memory alloys well suited to spectacle (glasses) frames?
options: They return to their original shape after being bent or deformed
They are much cheaper than ordinary steel
They glow so the glasses can be seen in the dark
They dissolve harmlessly if they are swallowed
questions.explain: Shape memory alloys can recover their original shape, so frames spring back rather than staying bent.

questions.q: Photochromic lenses are used in sunglasses because they:
options: Darken automatically in bright ultraviolet light and clear indoors
Warm up to keep the eyes comfortable in cold weather
Change colour when the wearer's temperature rises
Conduct electricity to power a small display
questions.explain: Photochromic lenses respond to UV light, darkening outdoors and becoming clear again indoors.

questions.q: Which property makes graphene particularly useful in electronic devices?
options: It is an excellent conductor of electricity while being extremely thin and strong
It is a good electrical insulator that blocks all current
It is heavy and dense, adding useful weight to devices
It is opaque and reflects all light that hits it
questions.explain: Graphene combines outstanding electrical conductivity with being very thin, light and strong, ideal for electronics.

questions.q: Metal foams are chosen for applications where a designer needs a material that is:
options: Lightweight but still stiff and good at absorbing impacts
Dense and heavy for use as counterweights
Transparent so components can be seen inside
Highly flexible and stretchy like an elastic band
questions.explain: Metal foams contain gas pockets, giving a low density yet high stiffness and good energy absorption.

questions.q: Why does a composite material such as GRP often perform better than its separate ingredients?
options: Combining the materials produces enhanced properties not present in either one alone
The materials cancel each other out to make a weaker, cheaper product
One material simply replaces the other with no change in properties
Composites always weigh more, which makes them stronger
questions.explain: A composite bonds two or more materials so the combination gives improved properties, such as fibres for strength in a supporting matrix.

questions.q: A breathable waterproof fabric such as Gore-Tex keeps rain out yet lets sweat escape because:
options: Its membrane pores are too small for water droplets but large enough for water vapour
It absorbs all the rain and slowly releases it back outside
It is coated in oil that repels both liquid and vapour equally
It heats up to evaporate any water before it can pass through
questions.explain: The membrane's tiny pores block liquid water droplets while allowing much smaller water-vapour molecules through.

questions.q: A baby's feeding spoon may use a thermochromic coating in order to:
options: Change colour to warn a carer when the food is too hot
Stiffen so the spoon cannot bend during feeding
Return to its original shape if the handle is bent
Conduct heat away so the food cools faster
questions.explain: Thermochromic coatings change colour with temperature, signalling when food is too hot for a baby.

questions.q: A designer wants a kettle that visibly shows the user when the water inside has become hot. Which material is most appropriate?
options: A thermochromic coating on the kettle body
A photochromic panel on the kettle body
A shape memory alloy handle
A carbon fibre reinforced polymer shell
questions.explain: A thermochromic coating changes colour with temperature, indicating when the kettle is hot.

questions.q: A manufacturer needs a racing bicycle frame that is both very strong and extremely lightweight. Which material best meets this requirement?
options: Carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP)
Metal foam
Thermochromic polymer
Ordinary mild steel
questions.explain: CFRP offers a very high strength-to-weight ratio, making it ideal for lightweight, strong bicycle frames.

questions.q: A client asks for spectacle lenses that automatically darken in bright sunlight and clear again indoors. Which smart material should be specified?
options: Photochromic material
Thermochromic material
Shape memory alloy
Graphene
questions.explain: Photochromic materials respond to UV light, darkening in sunlight and clearing indoors.

questions.q: A dental company wants a brace wire that gently returns to a set shape at body temperature to move teeth. Which material is the best choice?
options: Shape memory alloy
Glass reinforced plastic (GRP)
Photochromic polymer
Metal foam
questions.explain: Shape memory alloys recover a remembered shape when warmed to their transition temperature, applying a steady corrective force.

specSource: AQA GCSE Design and Technology (8552) specification; Developments in New Materials
